newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere at 8-week high in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere at 8-week high in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere shares rose to their highest levels in eight weeks on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Tuesday on increased turnover.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce continued surging to a new record high while the two other listed banks were unchanged.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.81 percent to 177.33. The LISPI general index climbed 0.73 percent to 92.14 and the BLOM general index rose 2.5 percent to 1004.12.
Total market turnover rose to 434,679 shares from 411,136 shares for a value of $5,113,737 against $4,366,352.
Solidere A rose to $11.5 from $11 while B reached $11.5 from $11.375. It was the highest price A shares have reached since May 13 and highest for B shares since May 12 when they traded at $11.75.
Turnover in Lebanon's biggest company rose to 218,726 from 197,898 on Monday. This compared with at total of 382,448 shares traded throughout last week.
The shares traded in very strong demand and almost all supply orders were executed.
"Everyone is excited about Solidere and I can understand why. It's got fundamentals and the stock is way undervalued," a broker, who wished not to be identified said.
BLC hit a new record of $21 from $20.5 and two blocs totalling 32,000 BLC shares traded on the bourse at $20.875 and $21.
Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $4.375 on turnover of 58,107 shares and a block of 65,600 shares traded on the bourse at $4.375.
Banque Audi was also unchanged at $27.5. A block of 7,316 shares traded at $26 on the BSE.
"Banks are moving into a period of sabilisation. This also explains the shift towards Solidere shares. What else is there on the market?" the broker added.
The BSE said on Tuesday it was halting from July 14 block trading on the floor of the three listed banks.
"The banks' stocks are very liquid and we prefer that they be put on the central market," BSE Trading and Information Manager Fouad Baalbaki told Reuters.
There was no trade in the four industrial firms, Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
